title: Love Language #4: Acts of Service
coreMove: Helpful action speaks love when it answers a spouse's valued request; demands, guilt, fear, and role scripts turn the same work into compliance.

exampleSpecs.audience: spouses noticing that early helpfulness vanished after marriage
exampleSpecs.stakes: name the lost service without turning it into an accusation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show courtship service displaced by a mother and father model after a radical change

exampleSpecs.audience: couples assuming all helpful tasks carry the same emotional weight
exampleSpecs.stakes: separate valued service from random usefulness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show washing dishes, cooking a meal, ironing clothes, and washing the car as different service dialects

exampleSpecs.audience: spouses who copied family roles without noticing the cost
exampleSpecs.stakes: choose a current spouse's need over an inherited script
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the mother and father model losing authority to a chosen act of service

exampleSpecs.audience: spouses confusing loving service with surrender to pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: protect love from guilt and fear tactics
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: distinguish a lover from a doormat when guilt, fear, and coercion enter the request

exampleSpecs.audience: couples tired of hearing the same complaint
exampleSpecs.stakes: find the need inside criticism before defensiveness takes over
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show criticism pointing toward the service that would fill the deepest emotional need

exampleSpecs.audience: service-oriented spouses still missing each other's dialect
exampleSpecs.stakes: honor effort while redirecting it toward the task that lands
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show washing the car, cooking a meal, washing dishes, and ironing clothes as non-identical dialects
